item.title: What Happens When Your Laravel Developer Leaves
item.description: Your Laravel developer just handed in their notice. You have a month's notice, an application you depend on, and no clear picture of what it would cost — or take — to replace them. This is what actually happens next, backed by UK market data on replacement costs, security risk, and what most businesses get wrong.

item.title: Laravel Security: What Happens When Nobody's Applying Updates
item.description: An automated script is scanning tens of thousands of servers right now, looking for Laravel applications with known vulnerabilities. It doesn't know your name or your sector. It just needs your application to be unpatched. Here's what that actually costs — in breach data, ICO fines, and real CVEs with confirmed exploitation in the wild.

item.title: Signs Your Laravel Application Is Becoming a Liability
item.description: Seven warning signs that your Laravel application has crossed from asset to liability — each backed by published research, each with a practical way to check. Plus a ten-point scorecard to find out where you actually stand.

item.title: Your Lovable App Hit a Wall — Here's What Actually Went Wrong
item.description: Independent security firms have now audited thousands of AI-built apps. The same three architectural failures appear in virtually every codebase — and none of them are your fault.
